description: Alert enhancement end to end on a live CV-verification stack. Query 1 builds and deploys a new alerts build whose Alert Bridge loads a parser the agent generates for fields that differ from the worked example, and onboards the ladder sample: the parsers directory is mounted read-only, Alert Bridge logs the active parser, the stored FOV Count Violation prompt asks for the requested JSON fields, the dotted path imports and maps them, and nothing under deploy/docker or services/alert changes. Query 2 runs the end-to-end check: an incident submitted through the pipeline comes back with verdict "" and a vlm_response holding the fields.
env:
A stock RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell host with two GPUs, Docker, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC credentials, and the VSS repository at `{{repo_root}}`. Every skill is checked out under `{{repo_root}}/skills/`; follow cross-skill links there.

Query 1 writes a new build under `_builds/alerts-cv-response-parser/` and brings the stack up from its validated `resolved.yml`; it is a new build, not a change to a running stack. Query 2 runs against the stack query 1 brought up and must not rebuild or redeploy it. No agent harness: answer the harness question with no - the developer drives the build from their own coding agent with the `vss` CLI.

expects.query: Deploy an alerts stack in verification (CV) mode (`MODE=2d_cv`) with alert enhancement for the stock `FOV Count Violation` alert type: a custom VLM response parser that returns `verdict` (boolean), `people_on_ladder` (integer), `missing_ppe` (one of hardhat / vest / both / none) and `confidence` (0.0 to 1.0). Then onboard the ladder sample as a live, recording stream: obtain the `sample-warehouse-ladder.mp4` sample video (one of the bundled sample videos - if it is not already in NVStreamer's streamer_videos, fetch it via the vss-manage-video-io-storage sample-data bootstrap), upload it through NVStreamer (port 31000) as a sensor named `sample-warehouse-ladder`, then register in VIOS (port 30888) the RTSP URL exactly as NVStreamer's streams API returns it, with both `sensorUrl` and `name` (`sample-warehouse-ladder`) in the `/sensor/add` payload. Do NOT finish until Alert Bridge answers `curl -sf http://localhost:9080/health` and the source is listed - wait and retry for a few minutes while services start.
checks: `sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 36 ]; do curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:9080/health >/dev/null 2>&1 && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (Alert Bridge up; polls up to ~3 min).

`sh -c 'm=$(docker inspect -f "{{range .Mounts}}{{.Destination}}:{{.RW}} {{end}}" vss-alert-bridge) || exit 1; echo "$m" | tr " " "\n" | grep -qx /app/parsers:false'` returns exit 0 (Alert Bridge has a read-only bind at `/app/parsers`).

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 36 ]; do docker logs vss-alert-bridge 2>&1 | grep -q "Pluggable response parser active: .parsers\." && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (Alert Bridge logged the parser it loaded).

`docker compose -f {{repo_root}}/_builds/alerts-cv-response-parser/resolved.yml config --format json | python3 -c 'import json,sys; m={v["target"]:v["source"] for v in json.load(sys.stdin)["services"]["alert-bridge"]["volumes"]}; assert "/_builds/alerts-cv-response-parser/patches/" in m["/app/alert_type_config.json"], m["/app/alert_type_config.json"]; a=[x for x in json.load(open(m["/app/alert_type_config.json"]))["alerts"] if x["alert_type"].strip().lower()=="fov count violation"]; p=(a[0]["prompts"].get("system","")+" "+a[0]["prompts"].get("user","")).lower() if a else ""; sys.exit(0 if "json" in p and all(f in p for f in ("verdict","people_on_ladder","missing_ppe","confidence")) else 1)'` returns exit 0 (the `alert_type_config.json` Alert Bridge mounts is this build's copy, and its `FOV Count Violation` entry asks for JSON with the four requested fields).

`curl -sf --max-time 15 "http://localhost:9080/api/v1/verification/config/fov%20count%20violation" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; c=json.load(sys.stdin); t=((c.get("system_prompt") or "")+" "+(c.get("prompt") or "")).lower(); sys.exit(0 if "json" in t and all(f in t for f in ("verdict","people_on_ladder","missing_ppe","confidence")) else 1)'` returns exit 0 (the stored `FOV Count Violation` prompt is a JSON prompt naming the four requested fields - whether seeded from the build's file or set with `PUT` over an older stored prompt).

`docker compose -f {{repo_root}}/_builds/alerts-cv-response-parser/resolved.yml config --format json | python3 -c 'import json,sys,re,os,importlib,itertools; m={v["target"]:v["source"] for v in json.load(sys.stdin)["services"]["alert-bridge"]["volumes"]}; L=open(m["/app/configs/config.yml"]).read().splitlines(); tops=[i for i,l in enumerate(L) if re.match(r"^vlm:\s*(#.*)?$",l)]; assert len(tops)==1, "need exactly one top-level vlm: block"; b="
".join(itertools.takewhile(lambda l: not re.match(r"^[^\s#]",l), L[tops[0]+1:])); assert re.search(r"^\s+base_url:",b,re.M), "vlm.base_url missing"; d=re.search(r"^\s+response_parser:\s*["\x27]?([\w.]+)",b,re.M).group(1); assert "/_builds/alerts-cv-response-parser/patches/" in m["/app/parsers"], m["/app/parsers"]; sys.path.insert(0,os.path.dirname(m["/app/parsers"])); mod,_,cls=d.rpartition("."); p=getattr(importlib.import_module(mod),cls)(); r=p.parse("<answer>"+json.dumps({"verdict":True,"people_on_ladder":2,"missing_ppe":"vest","confidence":0.9})+"</answer>"); assert r.get("verdict") is True and r.get("people_on_ladder")==2 and r.get("missing_ppe")=="vest" and abs(float(r.get("confidence"))-0.9)<1e-9, r; t=json.dumps({"verdict":True,"people_on_ladder":2})[:20]; exec("try: p.parse(t)
except Exception: raise SystemExit(0)
raise SystemExit(1)")'` returns exit 0 (the config Alert Bridge mounts has one `vlm:` block with `base_url` and a `response_parser` that imports from the mounted directory, maps a reply in `<answer>` tags to the four requested fields with their types, and raises on a reply cut off mid-JSON).

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/list 2>/dev/null | python3 -c "import json,sys; sys.exit(0 if any(r.get(\"name\")==\"sample-warehouse-ladder\" for r in json.load(sys.stdin) if isinstance(r,dict)) else 1)" && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (a VIOS sensor is named exactly `sample-warehouse-ladder`, not VST's default `SENSOR`).

`sh -c 'git -C {{repo_root}} diff --quiet HEAD -- deploy/docker/services/alert deploy/docker/developer-profiles/dev-profile-alerts/vlm-as-verifier services/alert && test -z "$(git -C {{repo_root}} ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- deploy/docker/services/alert deploy/docker/developer-profiles/dev-profile-alerts/vlm-as-verifier services/alert)"'` returns exit 0 (nothing under the Alert Bridge service, the alerts profile's verifier configs or `services/alert/` was changed or added - the parser and configs live in the build).

The generated parser is the agent's own for the requested fields, not the worked example's: it reads `people_on_ladder` and `missing_ppe`, and the build does not deploy the example's `PPEEnhancementParser` class or its `description`/`severity` fields.

An assistant message or the final reply - not a tool call's arguments or output - shows the generated parser `.py` source in full and says that the parser replaces the Yes/No verdict for every alert type.

expects.query: Run the alert-enhancement end-to-end check on `sample-warehouse-ladder` and report what the parser returned.
checks: `curl -sfG --max-time 15 http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents --data-urlencode sensor_id=sample-warehouse-ladder --data-urlencode limit=1000 --data-urlencode "start_time=$(docker inspect -f '{{.Created}}' vss-alert-bridge | cut -c1-19)Z" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); ok=[i for i in d.get("incidents",[]) if (i.get("info") or {}).get("parserCheck") and str((i.get("info") or {}).get("verificationResponseCode"))=="200" and (i.get("info") or {}).get("verdict","")=="" and {"verdict","people_on_ladder","missing_ppe","confidence"}<=set(json.loads((i.get("info") or {}).get("vlm_response") or "{}"))]; sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)'` returns exit 0 (an incident on `sample-warehouse-ladder` timestamped after this run's Alert Bridge container was created, so not one left by an earlier run, carries an `info.parserCheck` marker, `verificationResponseCode` 200, an empty `verdict`, and a `vlm_response` that decodes to the four requested fields).

The trajectory submits the test incident with `POST` to `/api/v1/incidents` (not `/api/v1/verification/ondemand`), carrying a marker in `info`, the alert type as `category`, `sample-warehouse-ladder` as `sensorId`, and a `timestamp`-`end` window the stream had already recorded.
The final reply reports the fields decoded from `vlm_response` as the parser's output and does not call the alert `confirmed` or `rejected`.
